cards.text: Chronicles doesn't open with "once upon a time." The very first word is a name: Adam. Then Seth, Enosh, and on down to Noah. No ages, no stories, just names, like the book walked in and started reading the guest list. It ends with Noah's three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

Next come the families that grew from Noah's three sons, spreading out across the earth. Two names stand out. Nimrod began to be a mighty one on the earth. And Peleg got his name because in his days the earth was divided. Imagine your name being the headline from the week you were born.

Then the list zooms in on one line from Shem: Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, and on down through Terah. And finally, after all those names, it lands on one you KNOW: Abram, that is, Abraham. Friend, I spent years counting dust in a junk drawer, and even I was ready for a familiar face.

Abraham's sons are Isaac and Ishmael. Ishmael has twelve sons, starting with his firstborn, Nebaioth. Then Keturah, Abraham's concubine, has six more sons, and Midian is one of them. That family reunion needs a BIGGER yard.
Isaac's sons are Esau and Israel, the man also called Jacob (Genesis 32:28). Then the list follows Esau's family, Amalek among them, and after that the family of Seir.

Last up: eight kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites. Same beat every time. A king dies, and someone reigns in his place. Then comes a list of Edom's chiefs, and that's the whole chapter, friend. You just walked from Adam to Abraham without breaking a sweat.
